---
title: Getting Started
---

Source code for hands-on is available in Fortran and Python.
The following environment is required to run the program.

## Fortran

Prepare a Fortran complier such as gfortran.
The distributed code compiles and runs with gfortran-15.2.0.
For matrix multiplication, intrinsic procedure `matmul` is used.
To compute matrix inverse, a linear algebra library is required.
Although [OpenBLAS](https://www.openblas.net/) may be installed, LAPACK in Rtools is used on Windows and Accelerate.Framework is used on Mac.

For visualization of data produced with Fortran programs, a graphics package is required. R scripts are included in the hands-on distribution.

## Python

Python is a generic programming language and relies on libraries to add functionalities.
Numpy provides mathematical functions and matrix manipulation.
Matplotlib is a standard visualization package.
The hands-on distribtuion was prepared with Python 3.14.7.

Participants unfamiliar with a terminal or an editor may install [Jupyter](https://jupyter.org/) (see [Windows](#sec-jupyter-win)、[Mac](#sec-jupyter-mac)) that allows to write a program and execute it from a web browser.

## Google Colaboratory

[Google Colaboratory](https://colab.research.google.com/) is a cloud service with a free tier for anyone a Google account.
The free version has a severer computational resource.
Note that a good network connection is needed.

The default is Python on CPU, but it can be changed to GPU or switched to R or Julia.

## Terminal

On Windows 11, instead of `cmd.exe`, Windows Terminal is the default terminal emulator.
If not installed, search and install in Microsoft Store.

Terminal.app on Mac is located in `/Applications/Utilities.` and Others in LaunchPad.

## Windows

On Windows, [winget](https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/windows/package-manager/winget/) allows a quick setup.

Instead of Windows PowerShell, installed by default, PowerShell 7 is used.
To install PowerShell, search `terminal` in Start Menu and add to Task Bar.
By default, old Windows PowerShell launches.
Type the following to install PowerShell 7.

```powershell
winget install Microsoft.PowerShell
```

The profile for PowerShell 7 is automatically created but need to set it to launch PowerShell 7 by default.
The downward arrow in the title bar to select settings or type Ctrl+,.
Select PowerShell in black (not blue) in Default Profile in Start Up and click Save in the lower right of the window.
![](images/powershell_default_profile.png)

### Install Python

Not need for Fortran.

```powershell
winget install Python.Python.3.14
```

In the new tab of Terminal, a path to `python` is automatically added.
To quit python, type `quit()`.

```powershell
PowerShell 7.6.4
python
Python 3.14.7 (tags/v3.14.7:823f032, Aug  5 2026, 10:51:32) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)] on win32
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> quit()
```

Install Numpy and matplotlib with `pip`.

```powershell
pip install numpy matplotlib
```

### Install Jupyter {#sec-jupyter-win}

Install Jupyter if neede.

```powershell
pip install jupyter
```

When Jupyter Notebook is launched, the default browser pops up.
The current directory of Terminal will be displayed in the browser on launch.
`cd` can be used to move to another diretory before launching Jupyter.

```powershell
jupyter notebook
```

### Install an editor

To write source code, an editor is used.
Install your favourite editor.

```powershell
winget install Microsoft.Edit
winget install Neovim.Neovim
winget install GNU.Emacs
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudioCode
```

For those never used any editors, [`Microsoft.Edit`](https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/windows/edit/) is recommended.
The tutorial for [Neovim](https://neovim.io/) can be launched by typing `:Tutor`.
That for `emacs` is accessible by setting a cursor to `Emacs Tutorial` and type enter.

### Install gfortran and R

R scripts are provided to visualize the data produced by Fortran binaries.
R is not needed if other tools are used, RTools is a convenient way to install gfortran and LAPCK because it includes MinGW-w64 as recommended by Numpy [Build from source](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/building/index.html).

```powershell
winget install RProject.R
winget install RProject.Rtools
```

To set the paths, edit the configuration file `Documents\PowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` (or OneDrive\Documents if the account is connected to a Microsoft account). Create `PowerShell` folder if it does not exist before editing.

```powershell
edit $profile
```

```powershell
Remove-Alias -Name R # <1>
$env:PATH += "$env:ProgramFiles/R/R-4.6.1/bin;" # <2>
$env:PATH += "C:/rtools46/usr/bin;" # <3>
$env:PATH += "C:/rtools46/x86_w64-mingw32.static.posix/bin;" <4>
```

1. In PowerShell `R` is an alias to recall the previous command. To avoid the name clash, remove the alias, allowing to type `R` instead of `R.exe`.
2. Path to `R.exe`.
3. Path to `make`.
4. Path to `gfortran`. Note that `x86_w64-mingw32.static.posix` depends on the platform and it is something else on the ARM64 architecture.

Open another tab to confirm gfortran.

```powershell
gfortran --version
```

## Mac

For hands-on, the official installer from python.org can be used.
Install Numpy and Matplotlib, optionally Jupyter using `pip`.

For Fortran users, follow the instructions below to insrall gfortran and R using MacPorts.

### Install MacPorts

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org/) is preferred to Homebrew becaue it provide a more robust and consistent environment.
The default install location of MacPorts is `/opt/local`.

Follow Installing MacPorts](https://www.macports.org/install.php).

Update OS and use the pkg installer for the appropritate OS version.
The installer append `/opt/local/bin` to PATH in `.zshrc`.


1. Install Apple's Command Line Developer Tools.

```zsh
sudo xcode-select --install
```

2. (Optional) install Xcode from App Store and agree the license.

```zsh
sudo xcodebuild -license
```

3. (optional) install `xorg-server` to use X11.

```zsh
sudo port install xorg-server
```

See `man port` or [documentation](https://guide.macports.org/#using).

### Install gfortran and R

gfortran is a part of gcc package.

```
sudo port install gcc15
```

To make different version of gcc coexist, the compiler is named `gfortran-mp-15` to include the version number.
By running

```zsh
sudo port select gcc mp-gcc15
```

make gcc15 default and an alias `gfortran` pointing `gfortran-mp-15` is created in `/opt/local/bin`.

For visualization, install R.

```zsh
sudo port install R
```
### Install Python

To install Python in MacPorts instead of the official binary, type the following command. Python is not required for the hands-on in Fortran. To make multiple versions coexist Python libraries has a version number as py314-numpy.

`python314` is installed in `/opt/local/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14`.

```zsh
sudo port install python314
```

As in the install messages, use `select` subcommand to choose the Python version to use.

```zsh
sudo port select python python314
```

Next, install Numpy and matplotlib.

```zsh
sudo port install py314-numpy py314-matplotlib
```
In fact `python314` will be installed as the dependencies to Numpy or matpotlib.

### Install Jupyter {#sec-jupyter-mac}

Jupyter can be easily installed from MacPorts.

```zsh
sudo port install py314-jupyter
```
